'''Joseph Wang''' (born 1948) is an American [[Biomedicine|biomedical]] [[engineer]] and inventor. He is a Distinguished [[Professors in the United States|professor]], [[Science Applications International Corporation|SAIC]] [[Endowed chair|Endowed Chair]], and a former Chair of the Aiiso Yufeng Li Family Department of Chemical and Nano Engineering at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. Wang currently serves as the director of the UCSD Center for Wearable Sensors and as the co-director of the UCSD Center for Mobile Health Systems and Applications (CMSA).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=SELECTBIO - Point-of-Care Diagnostics and Biosensors 2021 Speaker Biography |url=http://selectbiosciences.com/conferences/biographies.aspx?speaker=340093&conf=POCDEC2021 |access-date=2023-01-03 |website=selectbiosciences.com}}</ref>

==Biography==
Joseph Wang was awarded a D.Sc. from the Technion<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joseph Wang {{!}} Jacobs School of Engineering |url=https://jacobsschool.ucsd.edu/people/profile/joseph-wang |access-date=2025-05-05 |website=jacobsschool.ucsd.edu}}</ref> in 1978 and subsequently worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research associate]] at the [[University of Wisconsin, Madison]] until 1980.<ref name=":2"/>

In 1980, Wang joined the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at [[New Mexico State University]] (NMSU), where he remained until 2004. During his tenure at NMSU, Wang was appointed [[Regents Professor]] and held the Manasse Chair from 2001 to 2004.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Joseph Wang |url=https://iem.ucsd.edu/researchers/people/profiles/joseph-wang.html |access-date=2023-01-03 |website=iem.ucsd.edu}}</ref>

From 2004 to 2008, Wang served as the director of the Centre for Bioelectronics and Biosensors at the [[Biodesign Institute]] and as a professor of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry, at [[Arizona State University]] (ASU) in Tempe, AZ.

In 2008, Wang joined the [[Jacobs School of Engineering]] at the University of California, San Diego ([[University of California, San Diego|UCSD]]), where he served as Chair of the Nanoengineering Department from 2014 to 2019.<ref name=":2" />

Wang founded the journal ''Electroanalysis'' (published by [[Wiley-VCH]]) in 1988 and served as [[editor-in-chief]] until 2018.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Akademisi |first=Türkiye Bilimler |title=International TÜBA Academy Awards 2022 {{!}} Türkiye Bilimler Akademisi |url=https://www.tuba.gov.tr/tr/news/about-academy/international-tuba-academy-awards-2022 |access-date=2023-01-03 |website=www.tuba.gov.tr |language=tr}}</ref>

Wang is a member of several academies, including the [[National Academy of Inventors|US National Academy of Inventors]] (elected in the class of 2022),<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Academy of Inventors |url=https://academyofinventors.org/fellows-list/ |access-date=2023-01-03 |language=en-US}}</ref> the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]] (EASA), the National Academy of Albania, and the [[Turkish Academy of Sciences]] (TÜBA).

Wang was ranked World #1 in multiple fields: Electrochemistry, Microrobotics, Bioengineering, Analytical Chemistry for lifetime citation impact in the 2026 ''Scholarly Index Top 1000 Scholars''.

Wang is a Fellow of the RSC, ECS, IUPAC and AIMBE, a recipient of the Heyrovsky Medal, the Talanta Medal, the IUPAC Medal and the Breyer Medal and holds an Honorary Professor from 9 leading universities in Spain. Czech Republic, China, Romania and Slovakia. He is the recipient of ACS Awards in Analytical Chemistry, Electrochemistry and Analytical Instrumentation.

== Fields of research ==
Wang's early research focused on electrochemical biosensors and detectors for clinical diagnostics and environmental monitoring, mainly on [[Blood sugar level|blood glucose]] monitoring for [[diabetes]] management.<ref>[http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/cr068123a blood glucose monitoring for diabetes management]</ref> His current research includes the development of [[nanomotors]] and nanomachines, wearable non-invasive sensors, electrochemical biosensors,<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/cr068123a | pmid=18154363 | volume=108 | issue=2 | title=Electrochemical Glucose Biosensors | year=2008 | journal=Chemical Reviews | pages=814–825 | last1 = Wang | first1 = Joseph| s2cid=9105453 }}</ref><ref>Chen, Chuanrui; Ding, Shichao; Wang, Joseph. (July 2023) "Digital health for aging populations" Nature Medicine.  29, 1623–1630 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02391-8</ref> [[bioelectronics]], microfluidic (“[[Lab-on-a-Chip]]”) systems, and remote sensors for environmental and security monitoring.<ref>[http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nn800829k man-made nanomachines]</ref>

Wang directed a team that combined efforts in the fields of [[biosensor]]s, [[bioelectronics]], and [[nanotechnology]] to fashion nanocrystals that can act as amplifying tags for [[DNA]] or protein biosensors. His work in the field of [[nanomachines]], involving novel motor designs and applications, has led to a fast [[nanomotor]],<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/tcr.201100031|title=Catalytically propelled micro-/nanomotors: how fast can they move?|first1=Wei|last1=Gao|first2=Sirilak|last2=Sattayasamitsathit|first3=Joseph|last3=Wang|date=March 3, 2012|journal=The Chemical Record|volume=12|issue=1|pages=224–231|via=Wiley Online Library|doi=10.1002/tcr.201100031|pmid=22162283|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the first demonstration of nanomotor operation in a living organism, embedding microrobots within oral pills,<ref>Mundaca-Uribe, Rodolfo; Askarinam, Nelly; Fang, H. Ronnie; Zhang, Liangfang; Wang, Joseph. (September 2023) "Towards multifunctional robotic pills" Nature Biomedical Engineering. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41551-023-01090-6</ref> motion-based DNA biosensing,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Motion-based DNA detection using catalytic nanomotors|first1=Jie|last1=Wu|first2=Shankar|last2=Balasubramanian|first3=Daniel|last3=Kagan|first4=Kalayil Manian|last4=Manesh|first5=Susana|last5=Campuzano|first6=Joseph|last6=Wang|date=July 13, 2010|journal=Nature Communications|volume=1|issue=1|page=36|doi=10.1038/ncomms1035|pmid=20975708|bibcode=2010NatCo...1...36W|doi-access=free}}</ref> nanomachine-enabled isolation of biological targets, such as cancer cell identification,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Micromachine-Enabled Capture and Isolation of Cancer Cells in Complex Media|first1=Shankar|last1=Balasubramanian|first2=Daniel|last2=Kagan|first3=Che-Ming|last3=Jack Hu|first4=Susana|last4=Campuzano|first5=M. Jesus|last5=Lobo-Castañon|first6=Nicole|last6=Lim|first7=Dae Y.|last7=Kang|first8=Maria|last8=Zimmerman|first9=Liangfang|last9=Zhang|first10=Joseph|last10=Wang|date=March 3, 2011|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=50|issue=18|pages=4161–4164|doi=10.1002/anie.201100115|pmid=21472835|pmc=3119711}}</ref> and advanced motion control in the nanoscale.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Joseph |last2=Manesh |first2=Kalayil Manian |date=2010-02-05 |title=Motion Control at the Nanoscale |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smll.200901746 |journal=Small |language=en |volume=6 |issue=3 |pages=338–345 |doi=10.1002/smll.200901746 |pmid=20013944 |issn=1613-6810|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Wang has also introduced the use of body-worn flexible electrochemical sensors for non-invasive [[biomarker]] monitoring and epidermal biofuel cells that harvest energy from sweat,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=Jayoung |last2=Campbell |first2=Alan S. |last3=de Ávila |first3=Berta Esteban-Fernández |last4=Wang |first4=Joseph |date=April 2019 |title=Wearable biosensors for healthcare monitoring |journal=Nature Biotechnology |language=en |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=389–406 |doi=10.1038/s41587-019-0045-y |pmid=30804534 |pmc=8183422 |issn=1546-1696}}</ref> including textile and epidermal-tattoo devices, touch-based fingertip sweat sensing, microneedle-based electrochemical biosensors for quantification of circulating [[metabolite]]s and [[electrolyte]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tehrani |first1=Farshad |last2=Teymourian |first2=Hazhir |last3=Wuerstle |first3=Brian |last4=Kavner |first4=Jonathan |last5=Patel |first5=Ravi |last6=Furmidge |first6=Allison |last7=Aghavali |first7=Reza |last8=Hosseini-Toudeshki |first8=Hamed |last9=Brown |first9=Christopher |last10=Zhang |first10=Fangyu |last11=Mahato |first11=Kuldeep |date=2022-05-09 |title=An integrated wearable microneedle array for the continuous monitoring of multiple biomarkers in interstitial fluid |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41551-022-00887-1 |journal=Nature Biomedical Engineering |volume=6 |issue=11 |language=en |pages=1214–1224 |doi=10.1038/s41551-022-00887-1 |pmid=35534575 |s2cid=248667417 |issn=2157-846X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He introduced multi-modal sensing platforms that offer simultaneous real-time monitoring of chemical markers, and vital signs such as blood pressure, [[Electrocardiography|ECG]], and [[Electroencephalography|EEG]]. Wang also introduced on-body microgrid systems for managing the power requirements of wearable sensor platforms. His work towards portable environmental and security sensor systems includes new 'green' bismuth electrodes for sensing toxic metals,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Joseph |last2=Lu |first2=Jianmin |last3=Hocevar |first3=Samo B. |last4=Farias |first4=Percio A. M. |last5=Ogorevc |first5=Bozidar |date=2000-07-01 |title=Bismuth-Coated Carbon Electrodes for Anodic Stripping Voltammetry |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ac000108x |journal=Analytical Chemistry |language=en |volume=72 |issue=14 |pages=3218–3222 |doi=10.1021/ac000108x |pmid=10939390 |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref> remote submersible devices for continuous [[environmental monitoring]], and a hand-held lead analyzer.

Wang published over 1300 papers on these topics that were cited over  200,000 times, leading to a H Index of 227.

==Published books==
* ''Stripping Analysis: Principles, Instrumentation, and Applications'' - 1985
* ''Electrochemical Techniques in Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine'' - 1988
* ''Biosensors and Chemical Sensors'' - 1992, with Peter G. Edelman
* ''Analytical Electrochemistry'' - 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th editions from 1994, 1999, 2006 and 2023, respectively
* ''Biosensors for Direct Monitoring of Environmental Pollutants in Field'' - 1997, with Dimitrios P. Nicolelis, Ulrich J. Krull, and Marco Mascini
* ''Electrochemistry of Nucleic Acids and Proteins'' - 2005, with [[Emil Paleček]] and Frieder W. Scheller
* ''Electrochemical Sensors, Biosensors and their Biomedical Applications'' - 2007, with Xueji Zhang and Huangxian Ju
* ''Nano Biosensing: Principles, Development and Application'' - 2011, with Xueji Zhang and Huangxian Ju
* ''Nanomachines: Fundamentals and Applications'' - 2013
